sources.title: Apollo 11 Technical Air-to-Ground Voice Transmission (GOSS NET 1)
sources.creator: National Aeronautics and Space Administration
sources.license_name: U.S. Government Work / Public Use Permitted
sources.extraction_locator_schema: NASA GET DD HH MM SS (mission elapsed days, hours, minutes, seconds)
sources.rights_note: NASA's Apollo 11 transcript index identifies the linked technical air-to-ground material as a raw transcript presented in its original form and states that no copyright is asserted. The NASA Technical Reports Server record identifies the document as a Work of the US Gov. with Public Use Permitted. This corpus uses the raw technical air-to-ground OCR transcript, not the copyright-corrected Lunar Surface Journal.
sources.extraction_method: Twelve manually selected, disjoint windows were faithfully transcribed from the NASA OCR HTML of the raw Technical Air-to-Ground transcript. Each window contains exactly ten consecutive timestamped transmissions in source order; no transmission was skipped within a window. Windows containing the transcript's three-dot garble marker or an ellipsis-only transmission were excluded. OCR spellings and the transcript's dash notation were preserved.

conversations.relationship_context: Apollo 11 Commander and Houston CAP COMM coordinating launch milestones during the first minutes of flight.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Apollo 11, Houston. You're good at 1 minute.

turns.speaker: CDR
turns.text: Roger.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Stand by for mode 1 Charlie.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: MARK.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Mode 1 Charlie.

turns.speaker: CDR
turns.text: One Charlie.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Apollo 11, this is Houston. You are GO for staging.

turns.speaker: CDR
turns.text: Inboard cut-off.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: We confirm inboard cut-off.

turns.speaker: CDR
turns.text: Staging.

conversations.relationship_context: Apollo 11 Command Module Pilot and Houston CAP COMM reading back a midcourse-correction PAD and coordinating battery charging.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Apollo 11, this is Houston. Mideourse correetion number 2. SPS/G&N 63059, plus 097, minus 020, GET ignition 02644 5792, plus 00118, minus 00003, plus 00177, roll 277 355 015, NOUN 44 BLOCK is NA, DELTA-VT 00213 003 00168, sextant star 30 2082 370.

turns.speaker: CMP
turns.text: Roger. Midcourse correction number 2. SPS/G&N: 63059, plus 097, minus 020 02644 5792, plus 00118, minus 00003, plus 00177 277 - Are you still copying?

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Roger. Still copying. Go ahead. Apollo 11, this is Houston. I copied your transmission about roll 277, and go ahead from roll 277. Over.

turns.speaker: CMP
turns.text: Roger. 355 015, NA, 00213 003 00168 30 2082 370. Vega and Deneb 007 144 068. No ullage. LM weight: 33302. Heads towards the Earth. Over.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: 11, this is Houston. Readback correct. Out.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Over.

turns.speaker: CMP
turns.text: Go ahead, Houston. Apollo 11.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Roger. We'd like you to terminate battery A at GET 26 hours and reinitiate battery A charge after midcourse correction 2. Over.

turns.speaker: CMP
turns.text: Apollo 11. Roger.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Roger. Out.

conversations.relationship_context: Apollo 11 crew and Houston CAP COMM sharing a television view of the lunar module hatch during translunar coast.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: 11, Houston. We can even read the decals up there on the LM hatch.

turns.speaker: LMP
turns.text: Well, let me zoom it up and see how much you can read.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Okay.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: We can see the LM umbilical connection quite well there, Buzz. We see you zooming in on one of the decals now. It's, "To reset, unlatch handle; latch behind grip and pull back two full strokes." That's about all we can make out.

turns.speaker: LMP
turns.text: Hey, you get an A-plus.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Thank you very much, sir. At least I passed my eye test.

turns.speaker: LMP
turns.text: I'm standing 6 feet from it, Charlie, and you can read it better than I can. There's something wrong with the system.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Roger.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: That's a real good view of the LM hatch handle there, 11. 0ver.

turns.speaker: CDR
turns.text: Roger.

conversations.relationship_context: Apollo 11 Command Module Pilot and Houston CAP COMM mixing informal crew banter with a technical accumulator-service request in lunar orbit.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Apollo 11, this is Houston. Over.

turns.speaker: CMP
turns.text: Go ahead, Houston.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: 11, this is Houston. We're showing you - -

turns.speaker: CMP
turns.text: The Czar is brushing his teeth, so I'm filling in for him.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Say again, please.

turns.speaker: CMP
turns.text: I said the Czar is brushing his teeth, so I'm filling in for him. What can we do for you?

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Roger. If you don't get in the way of the Czar while he's brushing his teeth, we'd like you to bring up the primary accumulator quantity a little bit. We're showing the quantity now at 20.6 percent on TM. Seems to have gone down a bit since you've gone into the shadow. We'd like it serviced to bring the quantity up to between 30 and 40 percent, preferable 35 percent. Over.

turns.speaker: CMP
turns.text: Okay.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: The computer is yours, 11. The loads are in and verified. You can go back to BLOCK.

turns.speaker: CMP
turns.text: We're in BLOCK.

conversations.relationship_context: Houston CAP COMM and Columbia relay a powered-descent GO to Eagle while the lunar-module crew manages communications and descent controls.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Eagle, Houston. If you read, you're GO for powered descent. Over.

turns.speaker: CMP
turns.text: Eagle, this is Columbia. They just gave you a GO for powered descent.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Columbia, Houston. We've lost them on the high gain again. Would you please - We recommend they yaw right 10 degrees and reacquire.

turns.speaker: CMP
turns.text: Eagle, this is Columbia. You're GO for PDI and they recommend you yaw right 10 degrees and try the high gain again.

turns.speaker: CMP
turns.text: Eagle, you read Columbia?

turns.speaker: LMP
turns.text: Roger. We read you.

turns.speaker: CMP
turns.text: Okay.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Eagle, Houston. We read you now. You're GO for PDI. Over.

turns.speaker: LMP
turns.text: Roger. Understand. AELD control circuit breakers. DECA GIMBAL AC - closed?

turns.speaker: CDR
turns.text: What?

conversations.relationship_context: Apollo 11 Commander and Houston CAP COMM confirming staging, ignition, and abort-mode capability during ascent.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: 11, this is Houston. You are GO for staging. Over.

turns.speaker: CDR
turns.text: Understand, GO for staging. And - -

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Stand by for mode IV capability.

turns.speaker: CDR
turns.text: Okay. Mode IV.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: MARK.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Mode IV capability.

turns.speaker: CDR
turns.text: Staging -

turns.speaker: CDR
turns.text: - And ignition.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Ignition confirmed; thrust is GO, 11.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Apollo 11, this is Houston. At 10 minutes, you are GO.

conversations.relationship_context: Apollo 11 crew and Houston CAP COMM establishing contact through Carnarvon and exchanging platform-alignment results.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Apollo 11, this is Houston through Carnarvon. Over.

turns.speaker: LMP
turns.text: Houston, Apollo 11. Loud and clear. Over.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Roger, 11. We're reading you the same. Both the booster and the spacecraft are looking good to us. Over.

turns.speaker: LMP
turns.text: Houston, Apollo 11. Would you like to copy the alignment results?

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: That's affirmative.

turns.speaker: LMP
turns.text: Okay. NOUN 71: we used 30 and 37, four balls 1; NOUN 93: plus 00016, plus 00033, plus 00152; GET 00 48 15; check star 34. Over.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Roger. Say again check star.

turns.speaker: LMP
turns.text: Check star 34.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Roger. We copy. And the angles look good.

turns.speaker: CMP
turns.text: And tell Glenn Parker down at the Cape that he lucked out.

conversations.relationship_context: Apollo 11 flight crew and Houston CAP COMM confirming translunar-injection readiness and radio coverage.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Apollo 11, this is Houston. You are GO for TLI. Over.

turns.speaker: CMP
turns.text: Apollo 11. Thank you.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Roger. Out.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Apollo 11, this is Houston. Over.

turns.speaker: CDR
turns.text: Houston, 11.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Roger. We'll be coming within range of the ARIA aircraft coverage, here, in about 1 minute. They're going to try uplinking both on S-band and on VHF this time. So if you turn your - make sure your S-band volume is turned up, we'd appreciate it. And we believe that we'll have continuous coverage from now on through the TLI burn. Over.

turns.speaker: CDR
turns.text: Very good.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Apollo 11, Apollo 11, this is Houston through ARIA 4. Radio check. Over.

turns.speaker: LMP
turns.text: Houston, we read you strength 4 and a little scratchy.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Roger. We're reading you strength 5, readability about 3. Should be quite adequate.

conversations.relationship_context: Tranquility Base crew and Houston CAP COMM communicating as Commander Neil Armstrong descends the ladder and first steps onto the lunar surface.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Okay. Neil, we can see you coming down the ladder now.

turns.speaker: CDR
turns.text: Okay. I just checked getting back up to that first step, Buzz. It's - not even collapsed too far, but it's adequate to get back up.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Roger. We copy.

turns.speaker: CDR
turns.text: It takes a pretty good little jump.

turns.speaker: LMP
turns.text: Okay.

turns.speaker: CDR
turns.text: I'm at the foot of the ladder. The LM footpads are only depressed in the surface about 1 or 2 inches, although the surface appears to be very, very fine grained, as you get close to it. It's almost like a powder. Down there, it's very fine.

turns.speaker: CDR
turns.text: I'm going to step off the LM now.

turns.speaker: CDR
turns.text: THAT'S ONE SMALL STEP FOR (A) MAN, ONE GIANT LEAP FOR MANKIND.

turns.speaker: CDR
turns.text: And the - the surface is fine and powdery. I can - I can pick it up loosely with my toe. It does adhere in fine layers like powdered charcoal to the sole and sides of my boots. I only go in a small fraction of an inch, maybe an eighth of an inch, but I can see the footprints of my boots and the treads in the fine, sandy particles.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Neil, this is Houston. We're copying.

conversations.relationship_context: Reunited Apollo 11 crew and Houston CAP COMM confirming cabin integrity, consumables, and computer readiness after lunar-orbit rendezvous.

turns.speaker: CDR
turns.text: Houston, this is Columbia. Reading you loud and clear. We're all three back inside; the hatch is installed. We're running a pressure check leak check. Everything's going well.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Roger, Eagle. Correction - Roger, Columbia. We copy. You guys are speedy; you beat us to the punch. We had a couple of things for you.

turns.speaker: CDR
turns.text: What are they?

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Oh, it was just - We wanted you to close the CO2 sensor breaker and give us an RCS onboard readout out of Eagle, but that's all. Columbia, Houston. We've got a state vector for you if you'll give us P00 in ACCEPT. Over.

turns.speaker: CDR
turns.text: Buzz says the CO2 sensor circuit breaker is IN

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Roger. Thank you very much.

turns.speaker: CDR
turns.text: The RCS quantity was approximately 60 at A and 45 percent at B.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Roger.

turns.speaker: CDR
turns.text: And we're going P00 in ACCEPT.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Roger. Thank you.

conversations.relationship_context: Apollo 11 Command Module Pilot and Houston CAP COMM discussing cabin moisture, passive thermal control, news, and a flight-plan update during the return coast.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Apollo 11, Houston. We were curious to see if there was any excess moisture up around the tunnel hatch area as we saw on 10. Over.

turns.speaker: CMP
turns.text: It just so happens that's what we were talking about now. There is a little bit of dampness around the outside edge of the hatch, but a very, very slight amount. We've got a hose up there that we're hoping will sort of help keep it a little bit dry.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Roger, Mike. Thank you much. Have you seen any more water collecting on the aft bulkhead? Over.

turns.speaker: CMP
turns.text: No, we haven't, as a matter of fact. It's been dry in that area since we got rid of that last time.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Roger. Thank you.

turns.speaker: CMP
turns.text: Apollo 11 is back in PTC attitude. Standing by for thruster quieting.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Roger. We see that. Thank you much, Mike.

turns.speaker: CMP
turns.text: Houston, Apollo 11. Could you get a little summary of the evening news for us?

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Yes, sir. We'll have it for you momentarily. Also, a little flight plan update, Mike. If you - On page 3 113, you can delete the O2 fuel cell purge. Over.

turns.speaker: CMP
turns.text: Will do.

conversations.relationship_context: Apollo 11 flight crew and Houston CAP COMM checking entry timing, spacecraft configuration, photography, and VHF antenna selection before Earth return.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Apollo 11, Houston.

turns.speaker: CDR
turns.text: Go ahead.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Roger. Just to get a little downlink here to check out our VHF: I show us about an hour and 37 minutes, approximately, from entry interface. Over.

turns.speaker: LMP
turns.text: Okay. That's about right.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Okay. Looks like we're together on that, and I guess we're standing by for you to whip into the entry attitude.

turns.speaker: LMP
turns.text: Okay. We've just been taking a couple of last minute pictures. We've finished the EMS entry check, primary water EVAP activation.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Roger. Mighty fine.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Apollo 11, Houston.

turns.speaker: CMP
turns.text: Go ahead.

turns.speaker: CC
turns.text: Roger, Mike. We recommend the left VHF antenna for VHF.
